title: Scopes and client credentials
summary: Scopes say what a client may do; claims say who someone is. Then issue tokens to services with the client credentials grant.

steps.title: Scopes are not claims
body: Two ideas that are easy to blur:

- A **scope** is a *permission the client asked for and was granted*: `orders.read`, `calendar.write`. The user (or an admin) consented to it. Scopes limit what **this application** may do on the user's behalf.
- A **claim** is *a fact about the subject*: `sub`, `email`, `roles: ["manager"]`, `tenant`.

A token for Ada's reporting app might carry `scope: "orders.read"` and `roles: ["manager"]`. The API should require **both**: the app was granted `orders.read`, *and* Ada as a manager may read orders. A user who is an admin doesn't make a read-only app an admin app.

Scopes travel as one space-separated string, in a claim named `scope` (RFC 8693, used by Auth0, Okta, Keycloak) or `scp` (Entra ID). Design them coarse enough to be understood on a consent screen and fine enough for least privilege: `orders.read` and `orders.write`, not `everything`.

steps.title: Machine to machine: client credentials
body: A nightly reporting job calls the Reports API. There's no user, so there's nobody to redirect. The **client credentials grant** is for exactly this:

- The client authenticates **itself**: `client_secret_basic` (the header above) or `client_secret_post` (`client_id` and `client_secret` as form fields). Stronger options are `private_key_jwt` (the client signs a JWT with its own key) and mutual TLS, and in Azure, **managed identities**, which have no secret at all.
- The token's `sub` is the client. There's **no refresh token**: the client just asks again.
- The server only grants scopes registered for that client, and fails with `invalid_scope` otherwise.
Store client secrets **hashed**. Because they are long random values, a plain SHA-256 is enough; slow password hashes are for human-chosen passwords.

steps.prompt: The token endpoint decodes a Basic header. What does this print?
steps.explain: Basic auth is base64 of `id:secret`. It's encoding, not encryption, which is why it is only ever sent over HTTPS. `Split(':', 2)` keeps any later colons inside the secret.

steps.prompt: A background service needs to call another API every hour with no user involved. Which grant fits?
options: Resource owner password, with a service account's password

steps.prompt: Check that a token's scopes include everything an endpoint requires.
code: bool HasScopes(string scopeClaim, params string[] required)
steps.explain: Split the space-separated string into a set, then every required scope must be in it.

steps.title: Scope checks
prompt: Write `bool HasScopes(string? scopeClaim, params string[] required)`:
- `scopeClaim` is space-separated and may contain extra spaces. `null` means no scopes.
- Return `true` when every required scope is granted. Comparison is exact (case-sensitive).
starter: bool HasScopes(string? scopeClaim, params string[] required)
solution: bool HasScopes(string? scopeClaim, params string[] required)
template: Dojo.Eq("one of several", true, HasScopes("openid reports:read reports:write", "reports:write"));
Dojo.Eq("two required, both granted", true, HasScopes("a b c", "c", "a"));
Dojo.Eq("two required, one missing", false, HasScopes("a b", "a", "z"));
Dojo.Eq("extra spaces are fine", true, HasScopes("  a   b ", "b"));

steps.title: A client credentials token endpoint
prompt: The starter registers two machine clients with hashed secrets and allowed scopes, and gives you `MakeJwt(object payload)` that signs an HS256 token. **Run checks** starts the server and calls it.

2. Authenticate the client from an `Authorization: Basic base64(id:secret)` header **or** from `client_id` / `client_secret` form fields. No credentials, an unknown client or a wrong secret -> `401 {"error": "invalid_client"}`. Compare the SHA-256 of the given secret with the stored hash using `FixedTimeEquals`.

3. `scope` (space-separated, optional): every requested scope must be allowed for the client, else `400 {"error": "invalid_scope"}`. No scope requested means all the client's scopes. The granted scope is the scopes joined by single spaces, in the order requested (or in the client's registered order when none were requested): `reports:read reports:write`.

4. Return `200 {"access_token", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 300, "scope"}`, where the token is `MakeJwt` of `{ iss = "https://auth.dojo", sub = <client id>, aud = "reports-api", scope, iat, exp = iat + 300 }`. Use `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()` for `iat`; the tests only check `exp - iat`.
starter: // Registered machine clients: id -> (SHA-256 of the secret, scopes it may request).
var clients = new Dictionary<string, (byte[] SecretHash, string[] Scopes)>
IResult OAuthError(string error, int status = 400) => Results.Json(new { error }, statusCode: status);
solution: // Registered machine clients: id -> (SHA-256 of the secret, scopes it may request).
var clients = new Dictionary<string, (byte[] SecretHash, string[] Scopes)>
IResult OAuthError(string error, int status = 400) => Results.Json(new { error }, statusCode: status);
if (id is null || secret is null || !clients.TryGetValue(id, out var client)) return OAuthError("invalid_client", 401);
var token = MakeJwt(new { iss = "https://auth.dojo", sub = id, aud = "reports-api", scope, iat = now, exp = now + 300 });
return Results.Ok(new { access_token = token, token_type = "Bearer", expires_in = 300, scope });
hints: `http.Headers.Authorization.ToString()` is empty when there's no header. Decode what follows `Basic ` and `Split(':', 2)`.
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await Dojo.TryAsync("Client authentication could be checked", async () =>
var wrongGrant = await Post(http, new() { ["grant_type"] = "password" }, null);
var noCreds = await Post(http, new() { ["grant_type"] = "client_credentials" }, null);
DojoWeb.Status("a wrong secret gets 401", 401, await Post(http, new() { ["grant_type"] = "client_credentials" }, "reporting-job:guess"));
DojoWeb.Status("an unknown client gets 401", 401, await Post(http, new() { ["grant_type"] = "client_credentials" }, "nobody:s3cr3t-value"));
DojoWeb.Status("one client's secret doesn't work for another", 401, await Post(http, new() { ["grant_type"] = "client_credentials" }, "audit-bot:s3cr3t-value"));
DojoWeb.Status("Basic credentials work", 200, await Post(http, new() { ["grant_type"] = "client_credentials" }, "reporting-job:s3cr3t-value"));

DojoWeb.Status("form credentials (client_secret_post) work", 200, await Post(http, new() { ["grant_type"] = "client_credentials", ["client_id"] = "audit-bot", ["client_secret"] = "another-secret" }, null));
await Dojo.TryAsync("Scopes and the token could be checked", async () =>
var tooMuch = await Post(http, new() { ["grant_type"] = "client_credentials", ["scope"] = "reports:read audit:read" }, "reporting-job:s3cr3t-value");
DojoWeb.Status("asking for a scope the client doesn't have gets 400", 400, tooMuch);
Dojo.Eq("the access token is a JWT", 3, parts.Length);
Dojo.Eq("signed with the signing key", sig, parts[2]);
Dojo.Eq("sub is the client id", "reporting-job", DojoWeb.Prop(payload, "sub"));
var all = await DojoWeb.Json(await Post(http, new() { ["grant_type"] = "client_credentials" }, "reporting-job:s3cr3t-value"));
Dojo.Eq("no scope requested -> all the client's scopes", "reports:read reports:write", DojoWeb.Prop(all, "scope"));
static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Post(HttpClient http, Dictionary<string, string> form, string? basic)
var msg = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "/oauth/token") { Content = new FormUrlEncodedContent(form) };
if (basic is not null) msg.Headers.Authorization = new System.Net.Http.Headers.AuthenticationHeaderValue("Basic", Convert.ToBase64String(System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(basic)));
